basis: Cerebellar malformation and retinopathy define the phenotype; renal cysts and polydactyly/syndactyly each occur in 2/3. Respiratory dysfunction is centrally mediated.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the nasopharynx; pharyngeal airways belong to the pulmonary axis.
Complex III deficiency causes metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia and hyperammonemia; pancreatic inflammation occurs in 1/2. Episodic confusion does not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Chronic bacterial infection with variable cervicofacial, thoracic and abdominopelvic sites; no individual axis has sufficiently established direct involvement across this umbrella.
Urushiol causes immune-mediated allergic contact inflammation of the skin.
Acquired infectious prions cause progressive central nervous system degeneration.
Primary microcephaly, abnormal cortical development and intellectual/developmental disability define this disorder.
Beta-globin deficiency causes microcytic anemia. Umbrella includes mild forms; skeletal/endocrine annotations chiefly reflect severe disease, and iron-related injury often involves treatment.
Ataxia results from pathology of the cerebellum, its connections or proprioceptive sensory pathways.
Hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma; acromegaly and associated cardiovascular diseases are separately diagnosed consequences.
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy with skeletal muscle necrosis, fatty replacement and proximal weakness; no established additional organ injury.
Inherited prion-mediated CNS degeneration causes dementia, ataxia and neuronal loss; visual dysfunction is predominantly central, and weakness does not establish muscle disease.
The supplied syndrome description defines severe limb shortening, glomerulocystic renal dysplasia and corneal opacities.
Autoimmune CNS demyelination; optic neuritis directly injures the optic nerve in roughly 30-50% over the course, although onset frequencies are lower.
Bacterial infection of the skin defines this umbrella; additional organ involvement depends on the specific infection.
Renal hypoplasia/azotemia, alopecia and severe developmental impairment occur in 4/4; contractures/genu valgum in 4/4. Hepatic steatosis (3/4) and eyelid hypoplasia (4/4) omitted at cap.
Defining arthritis/urethritis; keratoderma/nail dystrophy annotated 80-99%. Oral lesions (80-99%) and iritis (30-79%) omitted at cap; conjunctivitis usually transient.
Cerebellar malformation, developmental impairment, hepatic fibrosis and ocular coloboma define COACH; nephronophthisis occurs in 5/12 (~42%).
Neonatal seizures, abnormal cerebral electrical activity, encephalopathy and persistent developmental impairment define the disorder.
Emery-Dreifuss disease is defined by skeletal muscle wasting, early contractures and cardiac conduction disease/atrial arrhythmias.
Disrupted cholesterol metabolism defines this broad metabolic umbrella; additional organ damage varies by subtype.
Ependymal tumor arising in the spinal cord.
Tumor arises in thoracic wall soft tissues/periosteum and may occupy pleura, which belongs to pulmonary; lung parenchyma is spared.
Hyperkeratotic thickening of palmar and plantar skin defines the umbrella; syndromic extracutaneous findings are subtype-dependent.
Autoinflammatory panniculitis/lipodystrophy; myositis/contractures and lipodystrophic dyslipidemia are common (~30%+), but subtype frequencies are unquantified.
